scores.claim_text: United Airlines Ventures invested $15.0M (Sept 2022) and received warrants for 2,722,536 shares at $0.01.
scores.supports: United Airlines Holdings (CIK 0000100517) own filings repeatedly disclose Eve Holding / Eve Air Mobility: 7 hits on 'Eve Holding' and 4 hits on 'Eve Air Mobility' — across multiple 10-Qs (Q1 2023 through Q1 2024), 10-Ks (FY2022 and FY2023), the 2023 DEF 14A, and an October 2022 8-K (which is consistent with the September 2022 subscription closing).
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext(cik=0000100517, term='Eve Holding') and (term='Eve Air Mobility')
scores.M_value: Eve Holding hits=7; Eve Air Mobility hits=4. Earliest 8-K=2022-10-18 (matches Sept 2022 transaction). Recurring 10-Q/10-K disclosure through 2024-04-17.
scores.interpretation: United independently and continuously discloses Eve in its own SEC filings — strong corroboration of the relationship and investment. Recurring presence across periodic reports indicates meaningful, ongoing related-party / strategic investment disclosure consistent with the $15M cash + $0.01 warrants structure described.

scores.supports: External brand-validation hits show 41 mentions of 'Eve Air Mobility' and 170 mentions of 'Eve Holding' across all SEC filers. Most hits are Eve's own filings, but UAL, Mercury Systems, Garmin, and a SPAC (Direct Selling Acquisition) appear as independent filers referencing Eve. The disclosure itself flags non-binding nature, so the claim is calibrated to LOI-based industry-standard backlog reporting.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext term=Eve Air Mobility and term=Eve Holding cik=null
scores.M_value: Eve Air Mobility total_hits=41; Eve Holding total_hits=170. Several non-Eve filers referencing the brand.
scores.interpretation: Recipe is named_counterparty_order, but Eve explicitly characterizes the pipeline as non-binding LOIs from 29 customers — this is a well-disclosed soft-backlog claim. With external SEC footprint >40 hits and a PUBLICLY listed strategic customer (UAL) verifiable in C1, the order-pipeline narrative is supported by the kind of footprint a real industry participant would have. Per heuristic 7 (1-3 mentions = PASS/MODERATE), a count this high is clear PASS. We do not attempt per-customer LOI verification because the disclosure itself acknowledges they are non-binding.

scores.claim_text: Operations in Melbourne, Florida (US aviation facility, alongside Embraer).
scores.supports: EPA FRS returns 0 facilities for 'Eve' in Melbourne FL — but per calibration heuristic 1 (offices/R&D/aviation test EXPECTED absent from EPA FRS) AND the EXPLICIT note that Eve uses Embraer's facilities royalty-free under the MSA/SSA, the Eve-name absence is non-signal. Querying the parent name returns 5 EPA-registered Embraer aerospace facilities in Melbourne FL — including 'EMBRAER AREA 1', 'EMBRAER ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY CENTER INC' (1400 General Aviation Dr), and 'EMBRAER EXECUTIVE AIRCRAFT' (3 sites on General Aviation Dr).
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities (Eve, FL, Melbourne) and (Embraer, FL, Melbourne)
scores.M_value: Eve in Melbourne FL: n=0. Embraer in Melbourne FL: n=5 (Area 1, Engineering & Technology Center, 3x Executive Aircraft sites all on General Aviation Dr).
scores.interpretation: Real, geo-confirmed aerospace complex on General Aviation Drive in Melbourne FL adjacent to Melbourne Orlando International. The 'Engineering & Technology Center' name is exactly the kind of facility that would host Eve's Florida operations under the MSA shared-services structure. Geo-coordinates cluster at lat 28.10-28.11, lon -80.64. Claim PASSES via parent-name lookup as anticipated by calibration.

scores.claim_text: Embraer S.A. (parent) provides $75.8M (FY2023) of related-party services under 15-year MSA/SSA; Eve has royalty-free access to Embraer IP and engineering organization.
scores.supports: EDGAR full-text search of Embraer ADR (CIK 0001355856) returns 0 hits for 'Eve Holding', 0 for 'EVE UAM', 0 for 'urban air mobility', 0 for 'eVTOL' — and crucially 0 for the term 'Embraer' itself. This indicates Embraer's filings (6-K furnishings; foreign-private-issuer 20-F) are not indexed in the EDGAR FTS pipeline used here, so absence is structural, not a signal. Per calibration heuristic 2 (foreign-issuer ADR: 0-2 mentions = NORMAL).
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext cik=0001355856 (Embraer ADR) for multiple Eve-related terms
scores.M_value: 0 hits across 4 search terms (Eve Holding, EVE UAM, urban air mobility, eVTOL); also 0 hits for 'Embraer' itself, confirming structural index gap.
scores.interpretation: EDGAR FTS cannot verify or contradict this claim because Embraer's 6-K/20-F filings do not appear in the index. Per the explicit calibration for foreign issuers, this is NOT a red flag. Indirect support exists: EPA FRS confirms Embraer's Melbourne FL aerospace operations (C3), and USPTO confirms Embraer's deep aviation IP estate (162 granted US patents — see C5). The MSA/SSA narrative is consistent with what a real Embraer subsidiary would receive. Marking UNVERIFIABLE rather than RED_FLAG because the data source is structurally unable to test FPI counterparties.

scores.claim_text: Eve has a technology and intellectual property portfolio in eVTOL / urban air mobility; royalty-free access to Embraer IP under MSA.
scores.supports: USPTO ODP returns 4 Eve UAM applications pre-cutoff: 2 GRANTED utility/design VTOL patents (US 11,643,199 'Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) Aircraft' granted 2023-05-09 with rich CPC coverage in B64C 27/26, B64C 29/0025, B64C 39/08; and design patent D1115657 'Vertical Takeoff and Landing (VTOL) Vehicle') plus 2 provisional applications from 2023 ('Integrated Aircraft Command' and 'Flight Control Command Source Management') — both UATM / flight-control-relevant. Embraer S.A. has 162 granted US patents pre-cutoff including aviation-relevant work (e.g. 'Autonomous Unit for Emergency Lighting System for Aircraft, eVTOLs, VTOLs and Rotorcraft' explicitly mentions eVTOL).
scores.M_value: Eve UAM: n_granted=2 (both VTOL-classified, evtol category=2), n_total=4 with 2 provisionals in flight-control. Eve Holding: 0. Embraer: n_granted=162 with explicit eVTOL-titled grants.
scores.interpretation: Eve's own granted-patent count is small (2) — consistent with a company spun out from a parent and operating only since 2022. But the patents that exist are squarely on-topic (VTOL aircraft architecture). Combined with Embraer's 162-patent aerospace estate — to which Eve has explicit royalty-free access under the MSA — the IP-portfolio claim is supported. No 'Nikola pattern' here (where the company claims 51 patents but 0 are in claimed categories). PASS, though Eve's standalone IP is modest and the substantive portfolio depth depends on the Embraer license.

scores.claim_text: $83.1M related-party loan receivable from EAH (Embraer subsidiary) at 5.97% maturing Aug 2024; $26.1M drawn of $101.2M BNDES facility.
scores.supports: Cannot independently verify the EAH loan via EDGAR (Embraer FPI structurally not searchable per C4 result). However the disclosure itself surfaces several issues worth flagging from the slice: (a) Eve has lent $83.1M of its own cash UPSTREAM to its parent's US subsidiary at 5.97% — at a moment when Eve is pre-revenue and burning $94.5M/yr; (b) the maturity is August 2024, just two months after our 2024-06-30 cutoff, which is a near-term liquidity inflection; (c) FY2023 cash burn $94.5M vs. cash $46.9M + securities $111.2M + EAH receivable $83.1M + undrawn BNDES $75.1M = ~$316M total liquidity — runway ~3.3yrs at FY23 burn rate, but only if EAH actually returns the $83.1M on schedule.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext cik=0001355856 ('EVE UAM'); already 0 (structurally non-indexed) — see C4.
scores.M_value: 0 hits but structurally inconclusive. Self-disclosed: receivable from related party = $83.1M; debt drawn $26.1M of $101.2M BNDES; net loss $126M; net operating cash use $94.5M.
scores.interpretation: The structural fact pattern — cash-poor pre-revenue subsidiary financing its parent's affiliate at 5.97% with maturity right at the cutoff — is a moderate yellow flag. Not a Nikola-style fabrication (the loan exists and was disclosed in 8-K Jan 2023). But it weakens the 'twelve-months-of-liquidity' assertion because liquidity is contingent on EAH timely repayment. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY because management's standalone liquidity story relies on a related-party receivable they cannot independently enforce, and Embraer's FPI status means external monitoring is impaired.

scores.claim_text: Entry-into-service in latter half of 2026 (FAA / global certification).
scores.supports: FAA type-certification timelines for new eVTOL configurations are not testable from public registries before the certificate is issued. Per the rubric, FAA cert claims are UNVERIFIABLE.
scores.interpretation: Per rubric exclusion (FAA cert / projections without counterparty are LOW priority and UNVERIFIABLE). Slice context confirms the eVTOL has only completed engineering simulations, subscale flights, wind tunnel and full-scale ground tests (NO crewed full-scale flight disclosed) — a typical risk for a 2026 EIS, but not a registry-recordable contradiction.
